clue.text: French novelist and musician got in a knot

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
a piper is a musician who plays the bagpipes

explanation.surface: A French writer and a musician tied themselves up in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knot' looks like a tangle, but it is a wading bird; 'got in' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a small wading shorebird belonging to the sandpiper family, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Ultimately explosive piece of satire

definitions.meaning: a small firework that fizzes before finally going bang
a short witty attack in writing, a lampoon

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hissing firework that bangs at the end and a short satirical lampoon.

clue.text: Patriotic principles stirring up extremes of tension in Somalia

indicators.note: stirring up mixes the letters that follow into a new order
extremes of picks the first and last letters of the word tension

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nationalist fervour is inflaming tensions in Somalia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' gives TN, the first and last letters of 'tension'; 'stirring up' then rearranges TN, IN and SOMALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationalism is devotion to one's nation and its interests, a set of patriotic beliefs.

clue.text: Two women quietly climbing ancient monument

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Di and Mary are two women's names
Mary is the second woman's name
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Two women are softly making their way up an ancient monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the whole run DIMARYP, giving PYRAMID.
explanation.definitionFit: The pyramids of Egypt are among the most famous monuments of the ancient world.

clue.text: Testing depth of pipes and fittings

definitions.meaning: sounding water by dropping a weighted line
the water pipes and fixtures of a building

explanation.definitionFit: Plumbing is sounding a depth with a plumb line, and also a building's system of water pipes.

clue.text: Some are for moderate improvement

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people favour gradual, moderate improvements to society.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is a change for the better, an improvement made to a system or institution.

clue.text: City game to withdraw embargo

indicators.note: to withdraw means the game's letters go backwards

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, the game
a ban is an official embargo or prohibition

explanation.surface: A city's sporting body pulls out, lifting a trade embargo.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, rugby union, is the game; 'to withdraw' sends it backwards. 'City' stands as an attributive noun, as in 'city life'.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the adjective for things of a city, as in 'city life' or 'urban life'.

clue.text: Out of bed, pie-eyed and edgy

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
pie-eyed and tight are both slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone up and about, drunk and on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means tense and nervous, much the same as edgy.

clue.text: Extra purchase referred to in speech

indicators.note: referred to in speech says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a buy is a purchase

explanation.surface: An additional item bought is mentioned in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter untouched, counted as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye in cricket is one of the extras, runs not credited to any batter.

clue.text: Position relative of Spooner to display part of helmet

indicators.note: Spooner signals that the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a pose is a position held
a niece is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative of the Reverend Spooner strikes a pose to show off a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of POSE and NIECE gives NOSE PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosepiece is the guard on a helmet that protects the wearer's nose.

clue.text: Loony avoiding front of Norwich express

indicators.note: avoiding means a letter is left out of the word for loony

parts.note: loony and nutter are both slang for a mad person

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of Norwich

explanation.surface: A madman steers clear of the front of a Norwich express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a train, but it is the verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to express it in words or sounds.

clue.text: Incompetence a French head displayed over part of poem

indicators.note: in an across clue, over places the headland after the poem section

parts.note: un is French for a
a fit is an old word for a section of a poem, a canto
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: A French leader showed incompetence over a stanza.
explanation.walkthrough: FIT, an archaic word for a canto, is a crossword favourite; NESS appears in place names like Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfitness is lack of the skill or qualities needed, the same as incompetence.

clue.text: Flowers cover wife leaving mature set of intellectuals

parts.note: blooms are flowers
to bury something is to cover it

indicators.note: leaving means the wife's letter departs from the word for mature

parts.note: to grow up is to mature

explanation.surface: Flowers cover a wife departing from a mature set of thinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bloomsbury Group was a circle of early 20th-century English writers and artists, including Virginia Woolf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bloomsbury Group was a famous London circle of writers, artists and thinkers.

clue.text: Old word a cavalryman used for "take a tumble."

parts.note: a verb is a kind of word
a lance is the weapon a cavalryman used

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned term a horse soldier had for falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbalance is to lose one's balance and fall over, to take a tumble.

clue.text: Accumulating space for posters here?

definitions.meaning: a large board by the road on which advertisements are pasted

explanation.walkthrough: A hoarding in Britain is a billboard, a large outdoor board for advertising posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding is amassing a store of things, and also the British word for a billboard.

clue.text: Gunner's aid showing wisdom after the event

definitions.meaning: the rear sight on a gun barrel, used for aiming
understanding only once something has happened

explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding gained looking back, and also the rear sight of a firearm.

clue.text: Goddess associated primarily with Northumberland

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word associated

parts.note: Northumberland lies in the north-east of England, so it is the NE

explanation.surface: A goddess linked chiefly with an English northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's northernmost county, in the north-east (THE NE); 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Party man briefly nursing pain in the neck

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as a nurse holds a baby
briefly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: James is a man's name
a bore is a tiresome person, a pain in the neck

explanation.surface: A partygoer briefly tends a stiff neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts JAMES to JAME, which then holds BORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large lively gathering or celebration, a party.

clue.text: Sounds off, possibly, in the theatre

definitions.meaning: the stage direction for sounds made offstage completes this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds off' reads as one phrase meaning to complain, but 'off' belongs to the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, and 'noises off' is the theatre term for sounds made offstage.

clue.text: Energy guinea pig possibly employed eating away

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a guinea pig is one example of a rodent

explanation.surface: An energetic guinea pig is used to nibbling away.
explanation.definitionFit: Erodent is a rare adjective meaning corrosive, wearing or eating away.

clue.text: Adequate vessel for king in story

indicators.note: for means the ship takes the place of the king

parts.note: a parable is a moral story
R is short for rex, Latin for king
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A good enough ship stands in for a king in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Replacing the R in PARABLE with SS gives PASSABLE; 'in' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means good enough, just acceptable, the same as adequate.

clue.text: Irishman holding university. degree, a university official

indicators.note: holding means the Irish name wraps around the letters that follow

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
BD, Bachelor of Divinity, is a degree

explanation.surface: An Irishman with a university degree becomes a college official.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdean is a deputy to a dean, an official of a cathedral or university.

clue.text: Fatigue of convict going with stream

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid or gas
lag is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: A prisoner goes with the flow, exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the tiredness that follows a long flight across time zones.

clue.text: As domestic servants were in a poet's early life

definitions.meaning: servants in a big house were called by ringing bells
the title of John Betjeman's verse autobiography of his youth

explanation.walkthrough: John Betjeman was a British Poet Laureate; this is the title of his book-length poem about his early years.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants were rung for from the house's bells; it is also Betjeman's 1960 verse memoir of childhood.

clue.text: Fish emitted noxious effluvium

definitions.meaning: gave off a bad odour, in the British past tense

explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small fish, and smelt is also the British past tense of to smell.

clue.text: Evangelist's words of dismissal to magician?

parts.note: go is said to send someone away
a speller is one who casts spells, a magician

explanation.surface: A preacher tells a wizard to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller is an evangelist, one who preaches or reads the Gospel.

clue.text: Little money once to take to court, some say

indicators.note: some say means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: A small sum used to be all it took to bring a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The sou was an old French coin of very low value, so a small sum of former times.

clue.text: Wise selector of numbers?

definitions.meaning: ... Wise, the British comedian of Morecambe and Wise
the machine that randomly picks winning Premium Bond numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like an adjective but is the surname of the comedian; Premium Bonds are a British government savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was a famous comic, and ERNIE is the computer drawing British Premium Bond prizes.

clue.text: Guy that's tense about conclusion of operation

indicators.note: about means the word for tense goes around the next letter

parts.note: taut means stretched tight, tense

indicators.note: conclusion of picks the last letter of operation

explanation.surface: A man who is stressed about the outcome of surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but here it is the verb to mock; 'that's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or mock them, much as to taunt is.

clue.text: Sign of achievement at judo that can't be built on?

definitions.meaning: a coloured belt worn as a grade in martial arts
protected countryside around a town where building is restricted

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the green belt is a ring of countryside round a city where new building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is a judo grade, and also protected land around a city where development is barred.
